weights.csoNote: HIGH-RISK (cardiac) features: syncope on EXERTION or when SUPINE, NO prodrome, palpitations immediately before, known structural heart disease, FHx sudden death. ECG/rhythm + echo (HR/rhythm captured in vitals).
weights.weightCitation: 2018 ESC Syncope Guidelines (Brignole M et al., Eur Heart J 2018); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Syncope can be the presenting feature of massive/submassive PE or of MI; do ECG + troponin; PE — pleuritic chest pain, dyspnoea, unilateral leg swelling/DVT signs.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2019 Pulmonary Embolism Guideline (Konstantinides SV et al.); ESC 2023 ACS Guideline (Byrne RA et al.); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Sudden severe (thunderclap) headache with transient LOC; CT then LP for xanthochromia.
weights.weightCitation: AHA/ASA aneurysmal SAH guidance; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Groups two catastrophes. Ruptured ECTOPIC pregnancy — a leading cause of maternal death in Uganda; any reproductive-age woman / missed period with abdominal pain + collapse needs a MANDATORY urgent pregnancy test. Ruptured AAA — UNCOMMON in sub-Saharan populations. Pinned on abdominal pain OR reproductive-age woman/missed period. 'Back/flank pain' (classic AAA) is not a token — abdominal pain is the proxy.
weights.weightCitation: RCOG ectopic pregnancy guidance; ESC 2014 Aortic Diseases Guideline; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: The commonest cause — typical prodrome (nausea, warmth, light-headedness), an UPRIGHT trigger (prolonged standing, emotion, pain, heat), rapid full recovery. Exertional or supine syncope is NOT vasovagal and demands a cardiac workup.
weights.weightCitation: 2018 ESC Syncope Guidelines (Brignole M et al., Eur Heart J 2018) (reflex/vasovagal); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Syncope on STANDING from a postural BP drop (lying/standing BP captured in vitals); causes — drugs (antihypertensives, diuretics), volume depletion (Uganda: diarrhoea/dehydration common), autonomic failure (diabetic autonomic neuropathy).
weights.weightCitation: 2018 ESC Syncope Guidelines (Brignole M et al., Eur Heart J 2018) (orthostatic hypotension); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: KEY DISTINCTION: LATERAL tongue-biting, PROLONGED post-ictal confusion, incontinence favour SEIZURE; rapid full recovery favours SYNCOPE. (Brief myoclonic jerks can occur in syncope — 'convulsive syncope' — and do not make it a seizure.)
weights.weightCitation: ILAE; Davidson's 24th ed (distinguishing syncope from seizure)

weights.dx: Severe anaemia / acute blood loss as collapse
weights.csoNote: Uganda: anaemia is highly prevalent (malaria, hookworm, malnutrition, heavy menstrual bleeding, sickle-cell, GI bleed) and a major cause of collapse/faintness. The Hb VALUE is the real trigger but is a lab not a token (PALLOR is the clinical proxy). ACUTE blood loss (GI bleed, ruptured ectopic, trauma) causes haemorrhagic shock. Given the anaemia burden, the CSO may prefer this UNCONDITIONAL (check Hb in every collapse).
weights.weightCitation: WHO anaemia & haemorrhagic-shock guidance; ATLS; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on the at-risk population (diabetes/sulfonylurea, and malaria — a Uganda hypoglycaemia cause). DEFG — the glucose VALUE in vitals is the safety net, captured for every patient. Hypoglycaemia is a LESS TYPICAL cause of TRUE brief self-recovering syncope (it does not spontaneously recover without glucose; usually an adrenergic prodrome). Kept conditional here, vs UNCONDITIONAL in the confusion pack where it is central.
weights.weightCitation: ADA Standards of Care 2024; WHO Guidelines for Malaria 2025 (hypoglycaemia in severe malaria); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on fever/malaria. Uganda: severe malaria and sepsis cause collapse via THREE mechanisms — hypotension, hypoglycaemia AND anaemia — so a febrile collapse needs a malaria RDT/smear, glucose (DEFG) AND Hb. Severe malaria needs IV artesunate; septic shock needs fluids/antibiotics.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines for Malaria (2025); Surviving Sepsis Campaign / Sepsis-3 (Singer M et al., JAMA 2016); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Overlaps 'Cardiac syncope' but flags the Uganda-specific mechanisms: RHEUMATIC valvular disease (common — mitral/aortic stenosis) and HYPERTROPHIC CARDIOMYOPATHY (young sudden death — exertional syncope + FHx sudden death + murmur). EXERTIONAL syncope is a cardiac red flag mandating ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY. Pinned on the exertional feature or a structural risk to avoid pure duplication with cardiac syncope. (A murmur is an exam finding, not a feature token.)
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2021 Valvular Heart Disease Guideline; ESC 2014 Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Guideline; WHO rheumatic heart disease guidance; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: A reflex (neurally-mediated) syncope triggered by a specific situation — cough, micturition, defecation, swallowing — with rapid recovery; benign, but confirm the trigger.
weights.weightCitation: 2018 ESC Syncope Guidelines (Brignole M et al., Eur Heart J 2018) (situational reflex syncope); Davidson's 24th ed
